review.title: Follow a person through the door
review.text: A badge reader checks a credential against the access policy. A controlled vestibule can restrict passage between two doors. A camera records events for review and an alarm alerts staff. These controls address different questions: who may enter, who actually entered, and who should respond? On a workstation, authentication verifies an identity. Authorization determines which actions that identity may perform.

review.title: Follow an identity through sign-in
review.text: A password and a PIN both use knowledge. A password plus a registered hardware token combines knowledge and possession. A fingerprint is an inherence factor. Count independent factors, not prompts. Windows Hello can use a device-bound credential unlocked by a PIN or biometric. Identity and access management (IAM) covers provisioning, changing and retiring access. Single sign-on lets a user authenticate once for multiple services. Zero Trust calls for evaluating identity, device and access context even on the office network. A short-lived code generated by an authenticator app using a shared secret and the current time is a time-based one-time password (TOTP). The device holding the secret supplies the possession factor.

review.title: Trace a file request
review.text: A local account belongs to one computer. A domain account can authenticate against a centrally managed directory. Windows compares the account and its groups with access control entries. Child files and folders can inherit entries from their parent. Direct local access to an NTFS file uses its NTFS permissions. Access through a share also requires the share permissions to allow the operation. If share Read and NTFS Modify are the only applicable grants, the user can edit locally but only read over the share.

review.title: Match Windows controls to the risk
review.text: User Account Control (UAC) prompts when a process requests elevation. Depending on policy, a standard user may need an administrator's credentials, while an administrator may be asked for consent. Inspect the requesting app and expected action before approving. Defender Antivirus examines files and behavior for malware. Windows Firewall applies traffic rules for the active network profile. Group Policy can apply settings consistently to managed users and computers. A security group can receive permission to a share. An organizational unit (OU) organizes directory objects and can set the scope of a linked Group Policy Object. Moving a PC into an OU can change its policies without granting the user access to the share.

review.title: Choose the encryption boundary
review.text: BitLocker protects a volume at rest, including against reading a removed drive. BitLocker To Go applies to removable data drives. Encrypting File System (EFS) protects individual files on NTFS using certificate-based keys. Back up recovery information according to policy. Once a volume is unlocked, Windows still uses permissions to decide who can open a file. Encryption on a network connection protects data in transit.

review.title: Limit how far an account can reach
review.text: Use standard accounts for routine work and separately authorized elevation for maintenance. Grant only the rights required for the task. For temporary workers, set an account expiration date and appropriate group memberships. Use distinct passwords, approved password management, automatic screen locking and physical protection for laptops. Disable unused services and guest accounts where appropriate. Verify a hardening change by testing both the protected resource and the user's legitimate task.

sources: Microsoft Learn: file security and access rights
Microsoft Learn: EFS key backup with cipher

cards.prompt: What question does authentication answer at sign-in?
cards.answer: It verifies that the requester controls the credentials associated with the claimed identity.

cards.prompt: Which factor category does a registered hardware security key supply?
cards.answer: Possession, or something the user has.

cards.prompt: What physical access control manages passage through two successive controlled doors?
cards.answer: An access control vestibule. It helps staff control entry to a restricted area.

cards.prompt: Under Zero Trust, how much access does an office network location establish on its own?
cards.answer: Location alone establishes no entitlement. Evaluate the requester's identity, device and requested resource.

cards.prompt: What is an access control list on a Windows folder?
cards.answer: A list of entries that describe rights for identities such as users and groups.

cards.prompt: Where does an inherited file permission originate?
cards.answer: It comes from a parent object and propagates according to inheritance settings.

cards.prompt: Which Windows feature provides certificate-based encryption for individual NTFS files?
Which Windows mechanism centrally applies workstation configuration settings in a domain?
cards.answer: Group Policy, commonly through Group Policy Objects linked to the relevant scope.

cards.prompt: What should determine the permissions granted to a support account?
cards.answer: The specific duties the account must perform. Grant the minimum access needed for them.

cards.prompt: What account setting ends a contractor's access on a known date?
cards.answer: Account expiration. Check that group access and active sessions are handled through the offboarding process.

cards.prompt: What control protects an unattended, signed-in workstation after an idle period?
cards.answer: Automatic session locking with authentication required to resume.

cards.prompt: Why disable an unused workstation service after checking dependencies?
cards.answer: It removes an unnecessary running component and can reduce exposed functionality.

quiz.prompt: The file server has already verified Maya's identity. Its decision about whether she may edit payroll is called ____.
quiz.explanation: Authentication established who made the request. Authorization evaluates the requested access.

quiz.prompt: A fingerprint belongs to the authentication factor category “something you ____.”
quiz.explanation: Biometric characteristics supply an inherence factor.

quiz.prompt: An installer requests administrative rights and Windows displays a consent or credential prompt. Which Windows feature is responsible? ____.
quiz.explanation: UAC mediates elevation. A prompt alone does not establish that the installer is trusted.

quiz.prompt: A technician must encrypt an entire removable USB data drive with Microsoft's BitLocker feature for removable media. Enter the feature name: ____.
quiz.explanation: BitLocker To Go protects the removable volume even if someone takes it to another PC.

quiz.prompt: A newly created file receives the access entries configured on its parent folder. This mechanism is permission ____.
quiz.explanation: Inherited entries help keep access consistent as files are added.

quiz.prompt: An inventory operator gets read-only access to the asset list and no account-management rights. This applies the principle of ____.
quiz.explanation: The permissions are limited to those required to perform inventory work.

quiz.prompt: The user's programs must keep running while an unattended desktop requires sign-in to resume. Configure an automatic screen ____.
quiz.explanation: Locking the session preserves the running applications while protecting access.

quiz.prompt: A temporary account should cease permitting new sign-ins at the end of a contract, even if its password is still valid. Configure an account ____ date.
quiz.explanation: Account expiration sets the lifetime of the identity independently of password expiration.

worksheet.prompt: A camera recorded two people entering on one badge swipe. Explain what the camera established and recommend a control that could manage passage at the doorway.
worksheet.key: The recording supports investigating who entered. A controlled vestibule or a guard verifying each entrant can limit passage. Reviewing video alone does not enforce one credential per person.

worksheet.prompt: Compare a password plus a second memorized code with a password plus a registered physical key. Identify the factor categories and explain which pair supplies MFA.
worksheet.key: The two memorized secrets are knowledge factors. A password plus a registered physical key combines knowledge and possession, so the second pairing supplies independent factors.

worksheet.prompt: Casey belongs only to Intake for this folder. Intake has NTFS Modify and share Read, with no other applicable entries. Casey edits directly on the server but cannot save through the share. Explain both results and identify the limited change to consider if remote editing is approved.
worksheet.key: Direct access uses NTFS Modify. A network edit also needs share permission to change data, so Read limits the remote session. Consider granting the approved group Change at the share after checking its scope; keep NTFS access restricted to the intended folder.

worksheet.prompt: A standard user gets an elevation prompt each time an unfamiliar updater starts. What should support inspect, and what should happen if the update is legitimate?
worksheet.key: Identify the executable, publisher, source and expected maintenance activity. Use an approved deployment method or authorized elevation after verification. Keep the employee's routine account standard.

worksheet.prompt: A technician needs to detect a malicious download, restrict an inbound connection on public Wi-Fi and distribute a workstation setting across a domain. Match a Windows control to each task and explain its role.
worksheet.key: Defender Antivirus detects and handles malware. Windows Firewall can restrict inbound traffic on the public profile. Group Policy can distribute the configuration to managed workstations.

worksheet.prompt: A seasonal worker needs one application for two weeks on a shared workstation. Propose three controls and explain what each protects.
worksheet.key: Grant only the application's required rights, expire the account at the end of the assignment and enforce an idle screen lock. These constrain privileges, account lifetime and use of an unattended session.

worksheet.prompt: Before a laptop goes into service, protect its internal SSD against offline reading if it is later stolen. A second user needs selected NTFS files encrypted. Choose a control and recovery material for each case.
worksheet.key: Enable BitLocker on the laptop volume before loss and securely store the recovery key. For the selected files, use EFS and securely back up the user’s EFS certificate together with its private key, or arrange for an authorized data recovery agent. Verify recovery before relying on either control.
worksheet.source: Microsoft Learn: EFS key backup with cipher

worksheet.prompt: A former supervisor moves to reception. Her domain sign-in must continue but the payroll folder must become inaccessible. What should change, and what two results would you verify?
worksheet.key: Review group memberships and remove obsolete payroll access, including any direct grant. Refresh the user's sign-in context as needed, verify that payroll access is denied and confirm that reception tasks still work.
worksheet.source: Application exercise: trace the user's effective access
